why: Inverts the slit test, counting open-floor cells a tank CAN enter instead of the ones it cannot. A slit is by definition a gap a shell crosses and no tank enters, so the inversion turns a measure of shell-only geometry into a rough restatement of legal area -- and it reads high everywhere rather than zero, which is the direction that looks like data. The control pair is two boards differing only in a hole's width (one cell against three), where the true answer moves from non-zero to exactly zero.
killedBy: mapgen quality measures: the gap taxonomy (issue #822) calls a one-cell hole a slit and a three-cell door not, changing nothing else
